holding_summary: Municipal ordinance restricting storage of petroleum and other combustible materials as a nuisance was a valid exercise of the police power; injunction against enforcement dissolved.
notes: Concerns storage of petroleum/combustibles as a fire nuisance; no lodging, boarding, or room-letting content.

holding_summary: Lessee's own reconventional filing could not be used to plead lis pendens against the lessor's prior suit to annul the lease for nonpayment of rent; judgment for lessor affirmed.
notes: Ordinary lessor/lessee rent-and-lis-pendens dispute; no facts about dwelling rooms, lodgers, or short-term letting.

holding_summary: Tenant of leased farmland liable in damages for holding over and waste, but entitled to reimbursement for improvements made before the lease under Civil Code article 500.
notes: Rural land lease with buildings/improvements dispute; not about letting rooms or dwellings for lodging.

holding_summary: Possessory action over ownership of a market-house and its revenues; plaintiff's possession and slander-of-title claim upheld against defendant who failed to prove title.
notes: Dispute over ownership/possession of a public market-house; no dwelling, lodging, or room-letting content.

holding_summary: Verbal permission to occupy land rent-free during the donee's lifetime created only a revocable tenancy at will, not a usufruct or other real right; parol evidence of the permission was admissible but not of title.
notes: Gratuitous occupancy of land (no rent/compensation involved); falls outside the corpus's compensated-occupancy scope.

holding_summary: Evidentiary dispute over ownership of a house and lot seized under execution; witness competency and parol proof of title rulings affirmed in favor of the party claiming ownership.
notes: Title/seizure dispute over a house; occupancy arrangement mentioned (rent-free occupancy for repairs) is incidental, not about lodging or boarding practice.

holding_summary: A municipal grant of a flatboat-landing privilege in one part of the levee did not repeal the ordinance prohibiting breaking up flatboats elsewhere in the city; injunction against unauthorized use of plaintiff's riparian property affirmed.
notes: Concerns flatboat landing/breaking-up ordinances on the levee; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding house content.

holding_summary: Lessee of a steamboat's bar-room, forcibly ejected by the boat's new owner, could not recover damages from the former owner/agents absent proof of conspiracy; warranty against eviction did not extend to the vendee's assault.
notes: Commercial lease of a steamboat bar concession; unrelated to letting of dwellings or lodging rooms.

holding_summary: Furniture in the leased premises was subject to the lessor's privilege for unpaid rent, but furniture belonging to a third party (the tenant's daughter) removed before seizure was not; verdict for the value of that furniture reversed for lack of proof of actual seizure.
notes: Dispute over lessor's privilege on furniture in a leased house; no discussion of lodging/boarding practice, duration, or characterization of the occupancy.

holding_summary: A curator ad hoc could not be validly appointed for a mortgagor who was only temporarily absent and had a domicile at his furnished lodgings where service could be made; mandamus granted to allow a suspensive appeal.
notes: Mentions the party's furnished rented rooms only to establish domicile for service-of-process/absentee purposes; procedural passing reference, not a holding on lodging's legal character.

holding_summary: Res judicata did not bar a second suit over the right to use two church pews because it sought only a life-use right, distinct from the earlier suit's claim of full ownership.
notes: Church pew ownership/use-right dispute; wholly unrelated to dwelling occupancy or lodging.

holding_summary: A police regulation authorizing the mayor to order removal of an occupant from a house of prostitution or assignation had not been triggered because the mayor had never issued such an order, so the occupant had not violated it and the recorder lacked jurisdiction.
notes: Regulation targets houses of prostitution/assignation under vice-suppression police power, not ordinary lodging or boarding houses letting rooms for pay; outside corpus scope despite selector match.

holding_summary: Municipal ordinance prohibiting Sunday liquor sales was a valid police-power regulation, not an establishment of religion; conviction reversed on the facts because an unauthorized porter, not the saloon keepers, made the sale.
notes: Concerns Sunday liquor-sale regulation; no connection to lodging, boarding, or room-letting.

holding_summary: Lessor who wrongfully used abusive legal process to eject a lessee before his yearly lease's disputed term expired was liable in damages for the harassment and loss caused.
notes: Ordinary residential house lease (whole house, disputed monthly vs. yearly term) and wrongful-eviction damages; no room-letting, lodging, or boarding-house doctrine.

holding_summary: Lessor's privilege for unpaid rent attached to all movables on a leased plantation regardless of whether they belonged to one or both partners in the farming venture; evidence of the partners' internal partnership terms was inadmissible against the lessor.
notes: Agricultural plantation lease and lessor's privilege dispute; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

holding_summary: Plea of res judicata should have been sustained against a widow's claim to community property already litigated in a prior injunction suit against a mortgage creditor; sheriff's seizure and sale to the creditor upheld.
notes: Community-property/mortgage-foreclosure dispute; passing reference to tenants paying rent to the sheriff is incidental, not about lodging practice.

holding_summary: Lessor was entitled to rent for the months a former lessee held over after the lease expired, but damages could not be extended further on speculation that the property would have remained hard to re-let.
notes: Standard commercial property lease holdover/damages dispute; no room-letting or lodging-house content.

holding_summary: Merchants who conspired to boycott drummers who patronized a hotel, in retaliation against the hotelkeeper, were liable in solido for actual and punitory damages for destroying the hotel's business.
notes: Hotel/innkeeping facts (transient guests at $2/day) are incidental to a business-tort/boycott claim; the court does not characterize or regulate the letting itself.
